newsitem.title: USA: Micron stock tumbles after analysts cut estimates.
newsitem.headline: Micron stock tumbles after analysts cut estimates.

text.p: Shares of Micron Technology Inc. extended their recent sell-off Wednesday after several more Wall Street analysts slashed the computer chip maker's rating and profit estimates.

Micron slid $7.31, or more than 14 percent, to $43.81 at mid-afternoon on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the biggest percentage loser and most active issue. The stock has fallen nearly 20 percent since hitting a 52-week closing high of $53.375 last Thursday.
The stock had already fallen sharply in the past few days as Wall Street investment houses have said they expect lower profits for the company.

Citing concerns about falling prices on 16 megabyte computer memory chips, both Merrill Lynch and Brown Brothers Harriman became the latest brokerages to lower their ratings on Micron Wednesday morning.
They said an industry shift to 64 megabyte chips would force Micron to play catch-up with other chip makers and result in a surfeit of older, 16-megabyte chips on the market.
"There are too many DRAMs (dynamic random access memory chips) being made worldwide relative to demand," said William Milton, an analyst at Brown Brothers Harriman.
"The current price which Micron is getting for 16 mb DRAM chips is about 30 percent lower than the average selling price in the May quarter," he said.

Milton also lowered his estimate for the company's fiscal fourth-quarter earnings per share to 42 cents, from an earlier forecast of 51 cents a share. Merrill Lynch analyst Tom Kurlack cut his quarterly earnings estimate to 59 cents a share from 70 cents a share.
In addition to computer chips, the Boise, Idaho-based company is a leading manufacturer of personal computers.
